_comment: Procedural lore fragments. carvings are found near landmarks; bottles float near the banks.
carvings: Seven lamps from the spring to the salt. Light one and you are never the first, never the last.
Here Ysolde waited for the ice to break. It broke on the ninth day. She was glad she waited.
The water is older than the valley. The valley is older than us. We are only visiting.
Two boats, one lantern, a long way to go.
Whoever reads this: the fishing is better on the far bank.
We built this for our children's children. Hello, children's children.
When the river turns gold, stop rowing. Just look.
Lamplighter's rule: never pass a stranger in the dark without a light.
Flood year. We moved the town uphill and the river followed us, curious.
The heron is the river's patience given feathers.
Under this stone: nothing. We just liked the view.
Some say the river circles the whole world and meets itself. We say: good.
The stars are lamps too. Someone lit those.
To the traveller with wet socks: dry them by the fire, not the lantern.
The mountains are the river standing up to look around.
Every lamp has a name. This one's is Patience.
In the year of the long rain we sang to the water and it sang back.
Follow the fireflies. They know where the good places are.
No map is finished. That is the best thing about maps.
Rest here. The river will wait.
bottles: If you find this, I'm fine! I'm on an island with very good fruit and I'm in no hurry. - M.
To whoever: the fish in the third lake are enormous. Bring a bigger net. - T.
I threw this from the bridge on my birthday. Happy birthday to you too, whenever it is.
Things I have learned on the river: 1. Always carry tea. 2. Herons are judging you. 3. It's worth it.
There is a cave behind a waterfall where the walls glitter. I didn't take anything. You shouldn't either.
My love, I'll be home when the maples turn. Keep the lamp lit. - R.
A recipe: one river trout, a sprig of mint, a fire, a friend. Serves the soul.
Help! I'm not in trouble. I just always wanted to write that on a message in a bottle.
The old ones say the Hidden River shows itself to those who carry four lights. I only have one. Maybe next year.
I counted three hundred and six stars before I fell asleep in the boat. Beat that.
Whoever finds this owes me one story. Tell it to the next person you meet.
If the water glows blue at night, stir it with your oar. You'll see.
Grandmother's advice: when in doubt, row towards the sunset.
This bottle has travelled further than I ever will. Lucky bottle.
Somewhere downstream there's a lighthouse that nobody lights. Someone should.
